Fetched the Folger reader for Hamlet 3.4 this run: Folger through-lines 2622 to 2625 read Refrain tonight, / And that shall lend a kind of easiness / To the next abstinence, the next more easy; / For use almost can change the stamp of nature, with 185 marked at 2621 and 190 at 2626, so 3.4.186 to 189 is right. Every word, the semicolon and the lineation match; the Folger brackets (pointed round the Folio tonight, square round the Second Quarto passages) are editorial sigla, properly dropped. One thing the editor should know: Folger prints no stop after nature, the sentence runs on into line 190 (And either … the devil or throw him out / With wondrous potency), so the closing full stop marks a cut at a complete clause. It is the customary cut in the reference books and adds no word, so I do not count it as minting. Speaker is Hamlet (to Gertrude) and is named. Source leads with the name, no dash, about 88 characters.
